messages:
james_acme: Hey team, after migrating to Redwood hosted API our OpenAI-style tool calls started failing. Getting 400/422 schema errors: \"Invalid args: expected object, got string\" and \"priority: \"high\" not in enum\". We thought the OpenAI compat shim would handle this. Here's the request body we send:
```json
{
  "model": "gpt-4o-mini",
  "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"Create a task"}],
  "functions": [
    {
      "name": "create_task",
      "parameters": {"type":"object","properties":{"title":{"type":"string"},"priority":{"type":"string","enum":["HIGH","MEDIUM","LOW"]}}}
    }
  ],
  "function_call": {"name": "create_task"},
  "tools": null,
  "tool_args": "{\\"title\\":\\"Fix bug\\",\\"priority\\":\\"high\\"}"
}
```
Error from Redwood: `422 Unprocessable Entity - priority: \"high\" not in enum` and `Invalid argument type for tool args: string`. We're on dedicated capacity. Any pointers?

maya_support: hey james — sorry about the trouble. quick q: are you calling the Redwood API with the OpenAI compatibility flag enabled, or are you using our native tool schema? do you have the failing request_id and any raw logs?

james_acme: request_id: req_0abc1234. We set `openai_compat: true` in the client config. attaching the smaller payload above — the client library is stringifying the args for us (we didn't expect that).

sam_engineer: thanks. two things to call out quickly: 1) enum mismatch — our validator expects exact enum tokens (in your function schema it's `HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW`) and `high` doesn't match. 2) args are being sent as a JSON string (`tool_args` is a string) — our compatibility layer expects the args field to be an object. some OpenAI SDKs stringify args when doing tool calls over certain transports, and we currently don't unstringify+normalize enums in that codepath.

sam_engineer: quick workaround you can try now — send the args as an object and use uppercase enum. example:
```json
{
  "model": "gpt-4o-mini",
  "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"Create a task"}],
  "functions": [{"name":"create_task","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"title":{"type":"string"},"priority":{"type":"string","enum":["HIGH","MEDIUM","LOW"]}}}}],
  "function_call": {"name":"create_task"},
  "tool_args": {"title":"Fix bug","priority":"HIGH"}
}
```

maya_support: if you can't change the client quickly, a temporary option is to set `permissive_enum_coercion: true` on the call (server-side flag) — that will coerce common lowercase enum values to their canonical token. we haven't documented it publicly yet but can enable per-request for customers. alternatively, unwrap the stringified args in your middleware before sending.

james_acme: we pass through raw user input so forcing uppercase in the app is tough. permissive coercion would help — this is blocking our deploy, marking as high priority.

sam_engineer: ack — escalating to eng-runtime. creating ticket INTERNAL-6789 with the req id and payload. liam_oncall can you pick this up? sounds like our openai_compat path isn't normalizing stringified tool args + enums.

liam_oncall: on it. i'll reproduce with the exact payload. preliminary note: our compat normalizer currently runs earlier in the pipeline and assumes args are objects; if the client stringifies them we skip normalization. will patch to attempt JSON.parse on tool args when allowed. opening a patch and will post ETA in ~30m.

eng-bot: deploy-bot: created branch `openai-compat-fix` and PR #4321 by liam_oncall — run tests & travis pipeline triggered.

maya_support: thanks everyone. looping in your CSM to coordinate a short-lived toggle if we need to enable permissive coercion for production. james, we'll update you as soon as eng posts a patch or a patch rollout is scheduled. in the meantime either unwrap the args on your side or ask us to enable coercion on the request_id above. :thumbsup:
